portal.meaning: Lowercase home.arpa apex or admitted alias under home.arpa. The DNS adapter strips trailing dots from the alias label and rejects the reserved label home.

lan-ip.meaning: Address accepted by Python ipaddress.ip_address and rendered as IP text. DNS aliases bind to home.arpa, not to this address.

aliases.meaning: Additional DNS names as string elements, comma-separated text or iterable object keys. Only names ending in .home.arpa are bound; these must pass the DNS alias label rule.

dry-run.meaning: Validate names and address and plan bindings without writing DNS aliases.

primitive.meaning: The certificate operation (constituent_lock), or error for the stop-level exception arm.

role.meaning: Normalized appliance profile used by the certificate operation.

changed.meaning: Whether the primitive reports a change; some failure paths may report partial effects.

dry_run.meaning: Whether the primitive returned a dry-run receipt; a refusal before planning can report false.

state_generation.meaning: Reported generation of the certificate state, or 0 when not available.

client_reinstall_required.meaning: Whether clients must reinstall trust for the reported operation.

aliases.meaning: Deduplicated normalized names after the primary name.

dns_names.meaning: Names eligible for DNS alias binding.

names_bound.meaning: Names bound successfully before any refusal.

dns_aliases.meaning: DNS adapter results, in attempt order, including a failed attempt when present.

dhcp_dns_applied.meaning: Whether at least one name was eligible and all DNS attempts succeeded outside a dry run.

dhcp_reservation_applied.meaning: No DHCP reservation is made by this stop.

dhcp_reservation.meaning: Reservation is only declared in the plan.

first_failing_boundary.meaning: DNS adapter refusal or diagnostic copied on a failed binding.

failed_name.meaning: Alias at the first failed binding.

plan.meaning: Ordered action names describing the proposed operation.

proof.meaning: Evidence named by the primitive for this outcome.
